user.title: MariaDB Export
user.description: Choose where the recorder history lives. Use the second choice when Home Assistant is still on the built-in SQLite database.

recorder.title: Recorder database
recorder.description:
The recorder is using `{database}` on `{host}` as `{username}`.

The password stays in the recorder configuration and is read again for each export. That account can write. A separate read-only user is safer. Submit to test this connection.

manual.title: MariaDB connection
manual.description: Type the MariaDB or MySQL server that stores the history you want to export. If the recorder uses {scheme}, that is not this form: enter the MariaDB server instead.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP. Official MariaDB add-on: core-mariadb. Database on another computer: for example 192.168.1.20. Leave blank only when you fill in Unix socket.
data_description.port: Leave 3306 unless you changed the MariaDB port.
data_description.database: Database name. The Home Assistant recorder default is homeassistant.
data_description.username: MariaDB user that can read that database. Example: ha_export.
data_description.password: Password for that user. Leave empty only when the account has no password.
data_description.unix_socket: Leave empty for a normal host and port. Fill this only when Home Assistant is on the same machine as MariaDB, for example /run/mysqld/mysqld.sock.
data_description.ssl: Turn on only when that server requires an encrypted connection. A local add-on usually stays off.

reauth_manual.title: Update password
reauth_manual.description: MariaDB rejected the account. Enter the current password.

reauth_recorder.title: Recorder password
reauth_recorder.description: Update the recorder database password in Home Assistant, then submit to try the connection again.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to MariaDB. Check the host, port, and that the server accepts this connection.
error.invalid_auth: MariaDB rejected the username or password.
error.unknown_database: That database does not exist or this user cannot see it.
error.missing_host: Enter a host or a Unix socket.
error.missing_database: Enter the database name. The usual name is homeassistant.
error.missing_username: Enter the username, for example ha_export.
error.invalid_port: Enter a port from 1 to 65535. The usual port is 3306.
error.invalid_export_dir: The export folder must stay inside the Home Assistant config directory.
error.invalid_limit: Enter a row limit from 1 to 2000000.
error.invalid_timeout: Enter a timeout from 0 to 86400 seconds.
error.invalid_url: The recorder database URL could not be read.
error.not_mariadb: The recorder is not using MariaDB or MySQL. A new Home Assistant uses SQLite. Enter the MariaDB host, database, and user in the fields below.

abort.already_configured: This MariaDB database is already configured.
abort.not_mariadb: The recorder database uses {scheme}, which is not MariaDB or MySQL. Close this dialog and choose Enter a MariaDB connection.
abort.recorder_missing: The recorder is not running, so there is no database URL to use. Close this dialog and choose Enter a MariaDB connection.
abort.invalid_url: The recorder database URL could not be read. Close this dialog and choose Enter a MariaDB connection.

data_description.export_dir: Folder inside the config directory. Type mariadb_export to keep the default. Files appear in that folder.
data_description.default_format: csv, json, or jsonl. Used when an export action does not set a format.
data_description.default_limit: Maximum rows in one export when the action does not set a limit. Example: 250000.
data_description.statement_timeout: Seconds before MariaDB stops a query. Type 0 to leave the query uncapped. Example: 900.
